subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted API vs current provider

Alex - thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our performance discussion:

- Goal: validate end-to-end p95/p99 for FinLytics' document-summarization flow (approx 512 tokens, streaming enabled)
- FinLytics current provider (your numbers): p95 ≈ 450 ms, p99 ≈ 1.8 s (measured at app server)
- FinLytics target: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 700 ms (client-side end-to-end)
- Throughput: sustained 150 req/s during business hours; peak bursts up to 400 req/s
- Concurrency: expected concurrent connections from app tier ≈ 20
- Streaming: partial token streaming required (UI shows partial answers as tokens arrive)

What we (Redwood) will provide:
- A short SLO test plan (attached) and a measurement guide to align on how p95/p99 are computed
- A PoC environment (hosted) with traffic shaping to mirror your workload
- Tracing hooks (trace-id) so you can correlate client-side timings with server traces

Next steps:
1) I'll send the test plan and measurement guide (attached).
2) Marissa will schedule a PoC window for the week of Aug 9 and request sample queries and a representative traffic profile.
3) Please confirm whether your p95/p99 numbers are measured at the app server (before CDN) or at the end-user client.

Attachments: finlytics-slo-test-plan.pdf

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director of Solutions
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted API vs current provider

Thanks Laura - quick clarifications:

- Our reported p95/p99 are measured at our app server (node that calls the model) - not at the end-user browser. Latency includes auth handshake and our proxy.
- For streaming, we care about time-to-first-byte for the UI (we want the first token within ~100-150 ms) and the final token for p95/p99.
- Authentication: we use mTLS edge + short-lived tokens; any additional auth handshake would add measurable latency. Can you confirm typical auth flow and overhead?

Happy to share sample logs and a small set of representative queries - will send privately (and loop in procurement separately).

—Alex
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted API vs current provider

Appreciate the details, Alex.

To confirm:
- We measure p95/p99 at the request completion point (when the final token is emitted) by default. For streaming-first-byte, we report time-to-first-token separately.
- Our hosted API supports mTLS and short-lived bearer tokens. Typical auth overhead for a warmed connection is sub-5 ms; cold TLS handshakes can add 40-120 ms. For PoC we'll suggest keeping persistent connections / HTTP/2 to avoid repeated handshakes.
- We'll include trace-id propagation examples in the attached measurement guide.

Attached: redwood-slo-measurement-guidelines.md (includes curl examples, client-side instrumentation, and a small load script you can run)

Proposed PoC plan:
- PoC window: Aug 9-13
- Target traffic: mimic 150 req/s sustained, with 5-minute bursts to 400 req/s
- Measurement points: client-side (your app server) and server-side (Redwood traces) - we'll correlate with trace-ids
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 700 ms for 512-token streaming flows; time-to-first-token median < 120 ms

Marissa will reach out to lock the schedule and request sample queries and an IAM contact for provisioning.

Thanks,
Laura

Alex - looping in next steps from engineering/PoC side.

Can you please:
- Share a sample of 50 representative queries (anonymized) by EOD Aug 6
- Provide an IAM user or service account we can use for the PoC (scoped and time-limited)

PoC config we'll provision:
- Concurrent connections: start at 20, ramp to 50
- Sustained throughput: 150 req/s
- Burst: up to 400 req/s for 5-minute windows
- Payload: streaming, ~512 tokens average per completion
- Measurement: client-side p95/p99 + server-side traces; we'll share dashboards and raw metrics

If procurement needs a statement of work or a short trial addendum we can send a one-page doc - CC'd procurement here.

I'll send a calendar invite for the PoC kickoff (30m) - proposed Aug 9 at 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
